# <span id="aanchor315"></span> Master Characteristics

[&lt;&lt; Back](Master%20Characteristics.md#Tabs) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Characteristic</a> \| [Analysis](Master%20Characteristics%20-%20Analysis%20Tab.md) \| [Contractual/Operational](Master%20Characteristics%20-%20Contractual-Operational%20Tabs.md)

## Characteristic Tab

Characteristics are a set of standards by which a meter is operated. They are datetime effective and are used to warn the user when a meter characteristic is imported for the meter that does not match the known master meter configuration.

When creating a new master characteristic, it will appear pre-populated with data from the current meter characteristic, including the start and end date. All fields can be edited. If values are selected which are different from the current meter characteristic, the user will be warned when the user saves.

The fields displayed will change based on the selected meter type.

Meter characteristics are compared to master characteristics upon import and edit.

<div class="procedure">

To create a master characteristic:

1.  Select the **Characteristics** tab and click **New**.

2.  Enter the **Effective From** and **Effective To dates**, which defines the dates for which the master characteristic will be effective. There can be multiple master characteristics for any meter, but their date ranges will not overlap. If the date range of a master characteristic is set so that it overlaps an existing master characteristic, the existing characteristic will be modified (or deleted if the new characteristic completely overlaps the existing characteristic) so that there is no overlap.
    <div class="example">

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

    Suppose that for meter number 01000, there is a master characteristic that runs from midnight on January 1, 2000 through midnight on January 1, 2003. Now suppose that the user creates a new master characteristic with a start date of midnight on June 1, 2002. Since this overlaps the original master characteristic from midnight on June 1, 2002 to midnight on January 1, 2003, the effective date of the original master characteristic will be changed to midnight on January 1, 2000 to midnight on June 1, 2002.

    </div>

3.  Check the **Compare to Characteristic** option. When checked, the meter characteristic will be compared to the master characteristic upon import or edit. If unchecked, validations against the master characteristics will not occur.

4.  Flag fields of interest by checking **Compare** or **Autocreate**.
    1.  When **Compare** is checked, FLOWCAL will compare the master characteristics against the imported or edited meter characteristics. If the values differ from one another, then an exception will be generated.
    2.  When **Autocreate** is checked, the existing master characteristic record will be split at the date of the new meter characteristic containing the new value for that field. This will help keep the Master Characteristics up-to-date and minimize the number of exceptions generated when a new meter characteristic is imported or edited. This is useful for fields such as the orifice plate where changes are expected.

5.  Click **OK** to save.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 605;height: 569;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Characteristic Tab Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Characteristic tab:

- **Data Source** - The Data Source field is an FYI field and is similar to an edit reason. In general, Master Characteristics are manually maintained from paper reports. You may receive paper Equipment Change reports, Annual Equipment Inventory reports, Meter Test reports, etc. Based on these paper reports, the Master Characteristics data will be edited; this field tracks the source of information used to make the edit.

  When EFM data comes in, if an exception is generated, it either means that a change was made in the EFM and not reported, or a change was reported on paper but not entered into the EFM.

- **Sample Taken** - Check this field to indicate that a sample has been taken. This indication can be used to manually verify that the analysis is eventually received from the lab.

</div>
